literal: Virtue called hill having climbed they who stood, anger, moment even, keeping is rare.
translation: The anger of those who have climbed and stand upon the hill of virtue will rarely last even for a moment.
modern: குணம் என்னும் மலையின் மீது ஏறி நின்றவர்களின் கோபம் ஒரு கணம் கூட நிலைத்து நிற்பது அரிது.
explanation: The couplet describes the nature of those who have achieved great moral heights. It compares virtue to a mountain ('குன்று') that the great ones have climbed and stand upon ('ஏறி நின்றார்'). Even if such elevated people experience anger ('வெகுளி'), it is impossible ('அரிது') for it to last even for a single moment ('கணமேயும்'). The word 'காத்தல்' usually means protecting or guarding, but here it takes the sense of retaining or sustaining the anger, showing that true greatness naturally dispels negative emotions instantly.
